item.title: ICE officer who shot Venezuelan man wasn't wearing body camera, sources say
item.description: The ICE officer who shot a Venezuelan delivery driver was not wearing a body camera at the time of the shooting, sources familiar with the investigation told CBS News.

item.title: Trump hosting Venezuela's acting president at dinner for world leaders
item.description: President Trump is hosting acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez at a dinner for world leaders while they are both in New York for the U.N. General Assembly. CBS News national correspondent Lilia Luciano has more.

item.title: Trump administration to welcome up to 17,500 more White South Africans as refugees
item.description: The Trump administration is planning to welcome up to 17,500 more White South Africans as refugees over the next 12 months. CBS News immigration correspondent Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose, autopsy finds
item.description: An autopsy by the Greenville County Coroner's Office determined Hayden Panettiere's death was due to an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl.

item.title: Ukraine ready to sign landmark drone defense deal with U.S., sources say
item.description: Sources tell CBS News that Ukraine is ready to sign a landmark drone defense deal with the U.S., as new details of Ukrainian technology helping defend U.S. bases in the Middle East come to light.

item.title: U.S., Iran hold talks as Trump weighs cutting a deal or driving Iran "into hell"
item.description: President Trump tells the U.N. he has a "big decision to make" on whether to make a deal or drive Iran "into hell."

item.title: Hurricane Polo grows into powerful Category 5 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensified in the Pacific off the southwestern Mexican coast, growing into a Category 5 storm. Here's the latest on its path.

item.title: Supreme Court stays out of custody dispute between California couple and surrogate
item.description: Justice Elena Kagan declined a request from a surrogate to intervene in a custody dispute with a California couple.

item.title: New book details race to escape Afghanistan as U.S. forces withdrew
item.description: Diana Kapp is co-author of "The Last Free Women," which details the bravery of women who escaped the Taliban regime to build new lives in America. She and Mursal Rahim, one of the Afghan refugees featured in the book, join "The Daily Report" to discuss their stories.

item.title: Man shot by ICE being detained with bullet still in his back, lawyer says
item.description: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, the 28-year-old Venezuelan national shot by an ICE officer on Sunday, said in a phone call on Monday that he's "not doing well."

item.title: Austin police release new video of Venezuelan man shot by ICE
item.description: The Austin Police Department on Tuesday released new video of the man shot by ICE in Texas over the weekend. CBS News' Jason Allen has more.

item.title: DOJ charges Utah postal worker for allegedly dumping mail ballots in trash
item.description: The Justice Department says a U.S. Postal Service letter carrier in Utah threw out more than 300 mail ballots that were being sent to voters for the state's June primary.

item.title: Increase in drivers passing stopped school buses leads to safety concerns
item.description: When a school bus stops to pick up kids, the other cars on the road are supposed to stop with it. But thousands of times a day, they do not. As Mark Strassmann reports, some areas have found a way to crack down.

item.title: Online sports bettor says gambling now is "like crack in the '80s"
item.description: A CBS News investigation into sports gambling found that companies like FanDuel push hard to keep gamblers engaged and wagering, even as their losses pile up. Jim Axelrod has more.

item.title: Grand jury declines to indict anyone in death of Nolan Wells
item.description: Nolan Wells, 18, was found dead after going missing following an outing with friends on Mississippi's Horn Island on the Fourth of July.

item.title: U.S. fighter jet crashes at air base in Germany, injuring pilot
item.description: The U.S. Air Base Spangdahlem said that the pilot ejected and was receiving medical care.

item.title: In U.N. speech, Trump threatens to "annihilate" Iran and defends foreign policy
item.description: President Trump said he could "annihilate" Iran while predicting that Tehran would make a deal to end the war after the U.S. midterm elections.

item.title: Nolan Wells' family unsatisfied with grand jury finding no cause for criminal charges
item.description: A grand jury found no cause for criminal charges in the death of Nolan Wells, an 18-year-old college football player from Mississippi who died during a boating trip with friends. His family is still looking for answers. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Trump uses U.N. speech to openly muse about attacking Iran
item.description: President Trump spoke at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, wondering aloud whether to wipe out Iran before his aides sat down for what he called a "good meeting" with a delegation from the country. Ed O'Keefe reports from the U.N.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere died of accidental fentanyl overdose, coroner reports
item.description: Actress Hayden Panettiere died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl and several other drugs, according to a coroner in South Carolina. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Second U.S. F-16 fighter jet crash in 1 week, this time in Germany
item.description: For the second time in less than a week, a U.S. F-16 fighter jet has crashed, this time during a training mission in western Germany, according to the military. They said the pilot ejected safely.

item.title: Brain chip, AI program help ALS patient communicate again
item.description: ALS robbed Terry Mandable of his ability to speak. But with an experimental brain chip and an AI-backed program that translates his brain waves into speech, he can communicate again. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Family tied to suspected Chinese spy gave $4.4 million to Gavin Newsom, other California politicians
item.description: A family tied to a suspected Chinese spy made $4.4 million in donations to California politicians, including Gov. Newsom, a CBS News investigation found. CBS News' Josh Boswell breaks it down.

item.title: Foreign policy expert breaks down Trump's "annihilation" threat to Iran at U.N.
item.description: President Trump suggested to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday that he could "annihilate" Iran. David Tafuri, a foreign policy commentator and former State Department official, joins "The Daily Report" to share his analysis on that and Mr. Trump's comments about artificial intelligence.

item.title: 2 Ole Miss students found dead with packaged kratom in their rooms, police say
item.description: Two students have been found dead at the University of Mississippi. They were found at separate locations, but with the same easy-to-find drug. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: What to watch for with midterm elections 6 weeks away
item.description: Congressional candidates nationwide are entering their final campaign push with midterm elections set to take place in six weeks. CBS News' executive director of elections and surveys, Anthony Salvanto, walks us through it.

item.title: Trump tells U.N. General Assembly he will either strike a deal with Iran or "annihilate" country
item.description: President Trump spoke about the Iran war in his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, telling diplomats that he might choose to "annihilate" the country. CBS News' Natalie Brand breaks it down.

item.title: 9/22: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump makes case for his foreign policy during address to U.N. General Assembly; New Jersey lawmakers debate data center moratorium.

item.title: "Looksmaxxing" influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts
item.description: Online personality "Clavicular," whose real name is Braden Peters, faces two felony charges and one misdemeanor charge. He denies the allegations.

item.title: 195,000 heated blankets recalled after dozens of burn injuries
item.description: The manufacturer has received hundreds of reports of blankets "smoking, melting or burning" due to overheating, according to a recall notice.
